headline: Revenue is up 21% yet losses are widening; with $8.4B of debt on a $1.2B equity value, the stock is a leveraged bet on fuel.
business: JetBlue is a low-cost carrier focused on New York (JFK), Boston and Fort Lauderdale, with Mint premium transatlantic flying. It is executing its JetForward plan and a Blue Sky loyalty partnership with United after its Spirit merger was blocked.
recent: Q3 2026 net loss of $257M ($0.68/share) vs $143M a year ago, despite revenue +21.1% to $2.8B; adjusted loss of $0.60 missed the -$0.55 consensus.
Fuel averaged $3.91/gal (+57%); operating margin -5.1%; nine-month net loss totals $823M.
Liquidity about $2.2B (including a $600M undrawn revolver) against roughly $8.4B of debt; Q4 RASM guided +18-22% at $4.64/gal fuel.
strengths: Strong unit-revenue momentum after Spirit's exit
Valuable Northeast slots and a premium Mint product
Partnership with United widens loyalty reach
risks: Net debt/EBITDA of 94x: EBITDA barely covers interest
Cash burn may force dilutive equity or costly debt
Most exposed balance sheet if fuel stays above $4.50
